dario: Heads-up — weird edge crash when loading our sampleapp that uses webpack Module Federation to remote-load a microfrontend that imports the JS SDK. Works in local dev HMR but production bundle fails in the edge runtime.

hana: Can you paste the runtime error?

dario: Error in logs after remote init: "SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'export'" pointing at the remote chunk that contains `export default` from the SDK. Strange because the SDK package.json has a `main` and `module` field.

greg: Module Federation can load remotely served bundles that need to match the consumer runtime form (CJS vs ESM). If the SDK ESM file got served but the host expects a UMD/CJS shape, you'll see unexpected token. Also TF: some CDNs or bundlers wrap remote entry as script (not module) so browsers/edge throw on `export` tokens.

dario: Repro: webpack 5 host app uses ModuleFederationPlugin remotes: { sdkRemote: 'sdk@https://cdn.example.com/sdk_remote_entry.js' } The remote bundle was built from the SDK dist/esm entry but the host page included the remote script as a traditional script tag (no type=module).

hana: Two quick fixes: 1) publish a UMD/compat build for the remote entry when consumers use script tag loading, or 2) serve the remote container as an ES module and load with `<script type=module>` (not always possible for older infra).

greg: On the package side, we should ensure the SDK ships three artifacts: dist/esm (native ESM), dist/cjs, and dist/umd (for remote-script/Module Federation use cases). Also add `exports` map so bundlers pick the right one. Example package.json snippet suggestion:
```json
"exports": {
  "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
  "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
  "browser": "./dist/umd/sdk.umd.js"
}
```

dario: Another wrinkle: TypeScript typings point at ESM shape (named exports + default) but the UMD build exposes a global `Redwood` which confuses IDEs. TS consumers get intellisense mismatch.

hana: Suggest shipping a small `umd.d.ts` that declares `declare const Redwood: typeof import('./dist/esm').default; export default Redwood;` and reference it via `types`/`typesVersions` so bundlers and IDEs have consistent shapes per entry.

greg: For Module Federation specifically, add a CI job that spins up a minimal host + remote build (webpack MF) and asserts the remote can be loaded both as `script` and as `module`. That would catch regressions where a new ESM-only change breaks MF consumers.

dario: For teams blocked right now: fallback is to consume the SDK via namespace import dynamic `const sdk = await import('redwood-js-sdk'); const Redwood = sdk.default || sdk;` from the remote before using it, or rebuild remote entry as UMD.

ci-bot: Created issue #523: "redwood-js-sdk: Module Federation / remote-script ingestion breaks when SDK publishes ESM-only build; needs UMD/exports/interop typings + MF smoke CI" and attached a tiny repro.

dario: I'll draft a PR to add a UMD target + conditional exports + interop d.ts and include a webpack MF smoke test. Will link the repro.

hana: Thanks — this was a subtle one that would bite customers using microfrontends.

dario: :thumbsup:
